chunk_text: Corporate Event Policy Venue Capacity The main event hall supports a maximum of 500 attendees. The training room supports up to 80 attendees. Catering Options Approved catering options include vegetarian meals, non-vegetarian meals, snacks, tea, and coffee. Special dietary requests should be submitted with the event request. Cancellation Policy Venue cancellation requests should be submitted to the administration team as early as possible. Cancellation charges depend on the timing and the terms of the venue agreement. Event Approval Events require an approved request containing the event purpose, expected attendance, venue requirement, and estimated budget.

Employee Leave Policy Annual Leave Eligible employees may request annual leave through the approved leave workflow. Managers review requests based on staffing requirements. Sick Leave Sick leave should be recorded through the employee leave system as soon as practical. Leave Records Employees should ensure that leave dates and approval status are accurately recorded.

Company Travel Reimbursement Policy Domestic Travel Employees travelling on approved domestic business trips may claim eligible transportation, lodging, and meal expenses according to the limits defined in this policy. Original receipts are required for reimbursable expenses unless a documented exception applies. International Travel International business travel requires prior approval from the employee's manager and the travel administration team. International reimbursement claims must include the approved travel request, itemized receipts, and the final travel itinerary. nomy-class airfare is reimbursable for standard business travel. Higher cabin classes require explicit prior authorization. Meals Meal reimbursement is subject to the applicable daily allowance. Claims above the applicable allowance require documented approval. Submission Travel reimbursement claims should be submitted within 30 calendar days after completion of the trip. The claim should identify the trip dates, destination, business purpose, and supporting receipts. Hotel Management System Application 3 Hotel Management System Software Requirements Specification 1. Abstract The Hotel Management System is a software application designed to automate and streamline the day-to-day operations of hotels, including room reservations, guest management, check -in and check -out processes, billing, staff management, and report generation. The system provides a centralized platform that helps hotel administrators efficiently manage resources, improve customer service, and maint ain accurate records while reducing manual effort and operational errors. This project demonstrates the application of software engineering principles in developing a comprehensive manageme

monstrates the application of software engineering principles in developing a comprehensive management solution, showcasing key concepts such as modular design, database management, object - oriented programming, and user-friendly interfaces. It enables hotel staff to perform various operational tasks efficiently, enhances the guest experience through faster service delivery, and provides management with real-time access to important business information, all within a structured and integrated system. 2. Existing System Before the introduction of computerized Hotel Management Systems, hotel operations were managed manually using paper records, registers, spreadsheets , or disconnected softwa

erations were managed manually using paper records, registers, spreadsheets , or disconnected software applications. These traditional systems lacked automation, centralized data management, and real -time access to information, resulting in inefficiencies and operational challenges. The problems found in existing systems include: 2.1 Manual Reservation Management Traditional hotel management relied heavily on manual booking processes, leading to: • Errors in room reservations and guest records • Double booking or overbooking of rooms • Difficulty in tracking room availability in real time 2.2 Inefficient Guest Management Older systems lacked centralized guest information management, causing

Inefficient Guest Management Older systems lacked centralized guest information management, causing: • Time-consuming guest registration processes • Difficulty maintaining guest history and preferences • Delays in providing personalized customer service 2.3 Limited Billing and Payment Processing Existing systems often handled billing manually, resulting in: • Calculation errors in invoices and payments • Delays in generating bills during check-out • Difficulty tracking payment status and transaction history

Nine classes are defined — User (manages authentication and system access), Room (stores room details and availability), Reservation (handles room bookings), Guest (maintains guest information), CheckIn (manages guest arrivals), CheckOut (handles guest departures), Billing (generates invoices and charges), Payment (records payment transactions), and Report (generates operational and financial reports). Hotel Management System Application 15 11.3 Sequence Diagram The Sequence Diagram captures the chronological message flow between the Customer, Receptionist, Hotel Management System, and Database across three phases: Reservation Phase (room availability checked, booking details submitted, reservation confirmed), Guest Service Phase (check-in, room allocation, and service requests processed), and Billing Phase (bill generation, payment processing, and check-out completion). The diagram illustrates how information is exchanged between users and the system to ensure smooth hotel operations and efficient guest management. Figure 11.3 — Sequence Diagram

Hotel Management System Application 16 11.4 Activity Diagram The Activity Diagram illustrates the overall workflow of the Hotel Management System. It begins with user login, followed by room reservation and availability checking. Once a room is confirmed, the guest checks in and can access hotel services during their stay. The system records services, updates billing details, and processes check-out. Finally, the bill is generated, payment is completed, reports are created, and the session ends. Decision diamonds are used to verify room availability and determine whether additional services are required before check-out. Figure 11.4 — Activity Diagram

Hotel Management System Application 20 14. Conclusion The Hotel Management System is an integrated software solution developed to automate and streamline various hotel operations, including room reservations, guest management, check -in and check -out processes, billing, staff management, and report generation. The system provides an efficient and centralized platform for managing hotel activities, improving operational productivity and customer service. The application manages guest records, room availability, reservations, billing transactions, and hotel services automatically, reducing manual effort and minimizing operational errors. It showcases how technology can be effectively utilized to improve the efficiency and reliability of hotel operations.
